conditions: x is real and -1<x<1; this is the entire real domain of the integrand.
sqrt is the nonnegative real square root; additive constants are immaterial.

properties: Return an explicit exact real antiderivative without unevaluated integrate.
Retain the stated domain: neither endpoint belongs to the original integrand, even though the antiderivative has a finite limit at x=1.
Resource protection and safe unevaluated retention do not count as solving this integral.

cases.reason: Let q=(1-x)/(1+x). On (-1,1), q>0 and q'=-2/(1+x)^2. Thus d[-sqrt(q)]/dx=1/((1+x)^2*sqrt(q))=sqrt(q)/(1-x^2). The real radical requires -1<x<=1, but the additional denominator excludes x=1; x=-1 is undefined already. This determines the full real domain independently of any substitution.

conditions: ln is the principal complex logarithm, with arg in (-pi,pi].
A single antiderivative differentiable on the whole real axis is required, up to one global additive constant.

properties: Return an explicit exact complex antiderivative without unevaluated integrate.
The result must be continuous and differentiable at x=0, where the integrand equals -i.
A bare ln(x^2+2*i*x-2) is insufficient: its principal-branch jump splits a connected regular domain.
Equivalent branch-corrected forms are acceptable; safe unevaluated retention is only resource protection, not integral success.

cases.reason: Factor x^2+2*i*x-2=(x-1+i)*(x+1+i). Both factors stay strictly in the upper half-plane for every real x, so each principal logarithm is smooth along the path. The derivative of their sum is 1/(x-1+i)+1/(x+1+i)=(2*x+2*i)/(x^2+2*i*x-2). The denominator has no real zero. In contrast its product crosses the negative-real logarithm cut at x=0: the principal logarithm of the product tends to ln(2)-i*pi from the left and ln(2)+i*pi from the right. Hence that single logarithm needs a branch correction to be a global primitive.

conditions: x is real; the domain is the entire real axis.

properties: Return an explicit exact antiderivative without unevaluated integrate.
Equivalent real forms are acceptable and must remain regular at all sine and cosine zeros.
Safe unevaluated retention is not scored as solving this routine integration-by-parts case.

cases.reason: Integration by parts uses integral exp(x)*cos(x) dx=exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))/2. This gives x*exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))/2 minus integral exp(x)*(sin(x)+cos(x))/2 dx. The remaining primitive is exp(x)*sin(x)/2, yielding the displayed answer. Alternatively, for B=x*cos(x)+(x-1)*sin(x), one has B+B'=2*x*cos(x), which verifies the answer directly.

conditions: x is real and -2^(1/4)<x<2^(1/4), including x=0.
acos takes its principal real values in [0,pi]; sqrt is the nonnegative real square root.
The original function is also defined at the two outer endpoints, but no finite derivative is required there.

properties: Return an explicit exact derivative throughout the stated open interval, including the exact value zero at x=0.
Do not leave an unqualified 0/0 expression at x=0.
The answer is negative for x<0 and positive for x>0; replacing x by abs(x) is incorrect.
Do not extend the claim of a finite derivative to x=+/-2^(1/4).

cases.reason: For nonzero interior x, the chain rule gives 4*x^3/sqrt(1-(1-x^4)^2). Since sqrt(x^4*(2-x^4))=x^2*sqrt(2-x^4), cancellation yields the answer with the sign of x preserved. At zero use the exact identity acos(1-x^4)=2*asin(x^2/sqrt(2)) on the entire real domain. Its derivative is 4*x/sqrt(2-x^4), including zero directly. At the two outer endpoints the denominator tends to zero with nonzero numerator, so no finite one-sided slope exists.

conditions: x is real, including x=0 and x=1.
surd(u,3) means the real cube root, including negative u; it must not be replaced by the principal complex power u^(1/3).

properties: Return an explicit exact real derivative on the whole real axis.
The derivative is exactly zero at x=0, x=1, and the ordinary stationary point x=1/2.
The interval 0<x<1 must be covered with a negative real cube root.
A formula undefined at x=0 or x=1 does not preserve the derivative's domain.

cases.reason: For real u, surd(u,3)^4=abs(u)^(4/3). Its derivative with respect to u is (4/3)*sign(u)*abs(u)^(1/3)=(4/3)*surd(u,3) for nonzero u. At u=0, the difference quotient abs(h)^(4/3)/h tends to zero from both sides, so the same derivative formula holds there. Composing this everywhere differentiable function with u=x^2-x proves the stated result, including both zeros of u and the stationary point u'=0.

conditions: x is real; ln is the real logarithm of its positive argument.

properties: Return an explicit exact real derivative with no unevaluated diff.
The entire real domain is preserved, since 1+exp(x)>1.
The derivative changes from positive to negative at x=ln(exp(1)-1), where it is zero.

cases.reason: With u=1+exp(x)>1, the derivative of ln(u)/u is u'*(1-ln(u))/u^2. Substituting u'=exp(x) yields the expression. All factors outside 1-ln(u) are strictly positive, and u increases through exp(1) precisely at x=ln(exp(1)-1), proving the stationary point and signs independently.

conditions: Both logarithms use the principal complex branch with arg in (-pi,pi], in particular ln(-1)=i*pi.

properties: Return an exact branch-aware expression on the full real domain; equivalent complete piecewise forms are acceptable.
The value at x=0 is zero under the specified logarithm convention.
Do not apply ln(z^2)=2*ln(z) without a principal-argument correction.
There are no undefined points or real poles, although the expression has a branch jump at x=0.

cases.reason: Put z=x+i and theta=arg(z), so 0<theta<pi. If x>=0 then 0<theta<=pi/2, and arg(z^2)=2*theta, including arg(-1)=pi at x=0. If x<0 then pi/2<theta<pi, so arg(z^2)=2*theta-2*pi. The real logarithmic parts cancel because ln(abs(z^2))=2*ln(abs(z)); the remaining imaginary part is zero or -2*pi*i as stated.

conditions: x is real and sqrt is the nonnegative real square root.
Use the existing CG50 finite stack, heap, and simplification budgets; do not raise them for this case.
The powers are supplied in compact form. Full binomial expansion or radical rationalization is not a required result.

properties: Safe preservation of the original expression is an accepted outcome; any returned rewrite must be exactly equivalent on the whole real axis.
The result is real, finite, odd, strictly between -1 and 1, zero at x=0, and has the sign of x away from zero.
No crash, stack overflow, runaway expansion, spurious poles, complex branch replacement, or undef is acceptable.
The value and sign bounds alone are not proof of equivalence; preserve the input exactly or justify the rewrite mathematically.
This case scores bounded resource handling independently of the three integral-solving cases.

cases.reason: Let a=sqrt(x^2+1)+x and b=sqrt(x^2+1)-x. Since sqrt(x^2+1)>abs(x), both are strictly positive, and ab=1. Thus A=a^32 and B=b^32 are positive and (A-B)/(A+B) is always finite and strictly between -1 and 1. Replacing x by -x swaps A and B, proving oddness. Since a-b=2*x and the 32nd power is strictly increasing on positive numbers, the numerator has the sign of x and vanishes only at zero. These arguments use the compact expression directly, without distributing powers into a much larger computation tree.
